Meniere's disease

One randomized pilot compared laser with betahistine in 20 people and reported symptom improvement in both groups. A single case report combined laser with electroacupuncture, so its symptom resolution cannot be attributed to PBM alone.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One randomized pilot compared laser with betahistine in 20 people and reported symptom improvement in both groups. A single case report combined laser with electroacupuncture, so its symptom resolution cannot be attributed to PBM alone.

Summary of the Evidence

Two publications are listed for Meniere’s disease: one randomized active-comparator pilot and one case report. There is no replicated sham-controlled evidence. The publications address different interventions and endpoints, and neither establishes improved hearing.

Human and clinical evidence

Teggi et al. randomized 20 people with unilateral Ménière’s disease to low-level laser therapy or betahistine, ten per group. Vertigo spell frequency and duration improved from baseline in both groups. Betahistine produced faster improvement by three months, and audiometry showed no statistically significant between-group difference (2008, DOI 10.1089/pho.2007.2186, PubMed). The study is a small active-comparator pilot rather than a sham-controlled test. Hsu et al. described a 62-year-old woman with 28 attacks over two months who received nine sessions of electroacupuncture plus laser over two months; attacks were absent afterward (2026). The combined intervention and single-patient design prevent attribution to laser or inference about average benefit. Neither report demonstrates improved hearing.

Animal evidence

No animal evidence was identified in the exact category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo evidence was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The pilot used 5 mW laser treatment for 20 minutes per day over six months. The case report used laser together with electroacupuncture across nine sessions; the report does not support transferring a laser-only dose estimate. Disease severity, co-interventions, session schedules, and follow-up differ, limiting generalizability.

Interpretation

One small active-comparator trial provides a preliminary vertigo signal but does not show superiority to betahistine or a hearing benefit. The combination case is hypothesis-generating only.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for vertigo control and hearing improvement
Publications and records2 publications.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Evidence consists of one 20-person active-comparator pilot and one combined-treatment case report. The pilot found improvement from baseline in both laser and betahistine groups, with faster improvement on betahistine and no significant between-group audiometric difference. The case cannot isolate laser from electroacupuncture. A larger sham-controlled trial should measure attacks and hearing separately.
